implantQuestionAnswers.question: Can my implant fail?
implantQuestionAnswers.answer: Implant failure is unlikely if the procedure is performed by an experienced doctor in a sterile environment, and if sufficient and appropriate bone is available. However, patient factors such as diabetes or heavy smoking can reduce the success rate.

implantQuestionAnswers.question: How long does it take to complete implants?
implantQuestionAnswers.answer: Extracting all teeth and placing 12 implants can be completed in one day, with the implant placement taking approximately 1-2 hours. Patients typically leave the clinic with a temporary prosthesis. A minimum 3-month waiting period is required for the implants to fuse with the bone, after which the construction of crowns takes about 2 weeks.

implantQuestionAnswers.question: I have no teeth, how many implants are needed?
implantQuestionAnswers.answer: For a completely edentulous patient, semi-fixed implant-supported and tissue-supported prostheses can be created with 2 implants in the lower jaw and 3 implants in the upper jaw. For completely fixed teeth, at least 4 implants per jaw are required, totaling 8 implants, with an average of 6 implants in the upper jaw and 6 in the lower jaw.

implantQuestionAnswers.question: What is an implant?
implantQuestionAnswers.answer: An implant is an artificial tooth root made of titanium, used to replace missing teeth. It is placed into the jawbone, and after a waiting period, porcelain teeth are attached to it.

implantQuestionAnswers.question: Will there be pain during and after getting an implant?
implantQuestionAnswers.answer: Local anesthesia is used during the implant procedure to numb the area, preventing pain. Post-procedure, some discomfort and pain are normal and typically last 3-5 days. These symptoms can be managed with antibiotics and pain relievers.

questions.question: What happens in the first session?
questions.answer: In the first session, we conduct a detailed assessment. We gather information about your medical history, complaints, and goals. We review imaging results such as MRI and X-rays, perform a physical examination, and create a personalized treatment plan.

questions.question: How long does the treatment process take?
questions.answer: The duration of treatment varies depending on the type and severity of the problem and personal factors. Progress is tracked weekly with regular assessments. While some conditions may improve in a few sessions, chronic problems may require longer-term treatment.

questions.question: Can I continue my daily activities during treatment?
questions.answer: Yes, your treatment plan is designed with your daily life activities in mind. We support you in maintaining your daily routine with a personalized exercise program and recommendations. Activity modifications are suggested when necessary.

questions.question: What conditions do you treat?
questions.answer: We provide services for a wide range of conditions including orthopedic rehabilitation (back pain, neck herniation, muscle injuries), neurological rehabilitation, posture disorders, sports injuries, and post-surgery rehabilitation.

questions.question: Do you provide home exercise programs?
questions.answer: Yes, we prepare personalized home exercise programs to support your clinical treatment. We track your exercises through daily reminders and a feedback system.

familySupport.question: Is family support important in neurological rehabilitation?
familySupport.answer: Yes, family support is one of the most important components of neurological rehabilitation. We provide training to families on patient care, exercise support, and motivation techniques. We support the process with home programs and care recommendations.

earlyIntervention.question: Is early intervention critical in neurological rehabilitation?
earlyIntervention.answer: Early intervention is very critical in neurological rehabilitation. The first 6 months are called the 'golden period' and intensive rehabilitation during this time yields the best results. However, benefits can also be seen from rehabilitation started later.

faq.question: How long does posture correction treatment take?
faq.answer: Treatment duration varies depending on the severity of your postural disorder and individual factors. Typically, initial improvements are seen within 4-6 weeks, with significant changes occurring over 12-16 weeks. For scoliosis treatment with the Schroth method, a longer treatment period of 6-12 months may be recommended for optimal results.

faq.question: What age group is suitable for posture correction therapy?
faq.answer: Posture correction therapy is beneficial for all age groups. We offer specialized programs for children (especially during growth periods), teenagers, adults, and seniors. Early intervention during childhood and adolescence often yields the best results, but adults can also achieve significant improvements in posture and pain reduction.

faq.question: Can posture correction help with chronic pain?
faq.answer: Yes, posture correction therapy is highly effective for chronic pain caused by postural problems. Poor posture often leads to muscle imbalances, joint dysfunction, and nerve irritation, resulting in chronic neck pain, back pain, headaches, and shoulder pain. Our comprehensive approach addresses these underlying causes for lasting pain relief.

faq.question: Is the Schroth method only for scoliosis patients?
faq.answer: While the Schroth method was originally developed for scoliosis treatment, its principles can be adapted for various postural disorders. However, for scoliosis patients, it remains the gold standard non-surgical treatment approach, offering three-dimensional correction and respiratory improvement.

faq.question: How do you assess my posture problems?
faq.answer: We conduct comprehensive postural assessments including visual analysis, postural photography, movement screening, and biomechanical evaluation. For scoliosis cases, we also review imaging studies and perform specialized tests to determine the type and severity of the curvature.

faq.question: Can I continue working during treatment?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Our treatment programs are designed to integrate with your daily routine. We provide ergonomic recommendations for your workplace, teach postural awareness techniques, and offer exercises that can be performed during work breaks to support your recovery.

modernLifestyle.question: How does modern lifestyle affect posture?
modernLifestyle.answer: Modern lifestyle factors such as prolonged sitting, excessive smartphone use, computer work, and sedentary habits significantly contribute to postural problems. 'Text neck' and 'computer neck' are increasingly common conditions. Our programs specifically address these modern postural challenges with targeted interventions.

prevention.question: Can postural problems be prevented?
prevention.answer: Yes, many postural problems can be prevented through proper ergonomics, regular exercise, postural awareness training, and lifestyle modifications. We provide comprehensive education on posture-friendly habits, workspace setup, and preventive exercises to maintain optimal spinal health.

exerciseProgram.question: Will I receive a home exercise program?
exerciseProgram.answer: Yes, every patient receives a personalized home exercise program with detailed instructions and illustrations. We also provide video demonstrations and regular program updates based on your progress. Consistency with home exercises is crucial for achieving lasting postural improvements.

technology.question: Do you use modern technology in treatment?
technology.answer: We utilize various modern technologies including postural analysis software, exercise apps for home program compliance, and specialized equipment for postural correction. However, we maintain a balanced approach, combining technology with hands-on manual therapy and personalized care.

originalFaq.question: Is manual therapy painful?
originalFaq.answer: Manual therapy is generally painless. Some mild discomfort may be felt during treatment, but it should not cause pain.

originalFaq.question: How many sessions are required?
originalFaq.answer: Depending on your condition, 6-10 treatment sessions are typically recommended.

pilates.title: Clinical Pilates
pilates.description: Strengthening and flexibility work through reformer and mat pilates.
pilates.subtitle: Services offered under clinical pilates
pilates.ctaText: Book an appointment with our expert instructors for pilates sessions.

whatIs.title: What is Clinical Pilates?
whatIs.description: Clinical Pilates is an exercise system applied under physiotherapist supervision and customized according to each individual's specific condition. Unlike traditional Pilates, it focuses on injury rehabilitation, posture correction, and functional movement development.
whatIs.point2: Exercise design specific to your medical condition

benefits.title: Benefits of Clinical Pilates
benefits.subtitle: Health benefits you will gain through regular clinical pilates exercises

item1.title: Core Strengthening
item1.description: Strengthens deep abdominal and back muscles, increasing spinal stability and reducing back pain.

item2.title: Posture Correction
item2.description: Corrects poor posture habits, preventing neck and back pain while promoting healthier body alignment.

item3.title: Flexibility and Balance
item3.description: Increases muscle flexibility while improving proprioception and balance, reducing injury risk.

item4.title: Stress Reduction
item4.description: Reduces stress and supports mental health through breath control and mindful movement techniques.

process.title: Treatment Process
process.subtitle: How your Clinical Pilates program progresses

step1.title: Detailed Assessment
step1.description: We analyze your physical condition, movement patterns, and goals

step2.title: Program Design
step2.description: A personalized exercise program is created and objectives are set

step3.title: Progressive Implementation
step3.description: Starting with basic movements, program difficulty is gradually increased

step4.title: Progress Monitoring
step4.description: Regular evaluations update the program and track improvements

whoCan.title: Who Can Benefit?
whoCan.description: Clinical Pilates is suitable for individuals with a wide range of health conditions. People of all age groups can benefit from programs designed specifically for their condition.
whoCan.imageAlt: Pilates participants of various age groups
whoCan.group1: Individuals experiencing back and neck pain
whoCan.group2: Patients with posture disorders and scoliosis
whoCan.group5: Elderly individuals and those with balance problems
whoCan.group7: Healthy individuals for one-on-one pilates sessions
whoCan.group8: Individuals with weight problems and those wanting to lose weight
whoCan.group9: People who work from home at desks

testimonials.title: Patient Reviews
testimonials.subtitle: Our patients sharing their Clinical Pilates experiences

testimonial1.name: Sarah M.
testimonial1.content: After a 3-month clinical pilates program, my chronic back pain that I suffered for years completely disappeared. My posture improved and I feel much more energetic.

testimonial2.name: Michael K.
testimonial2.content: Clinical pilates was very helpful during my post-surgery rehabilitation process. I feel strong both physically and mentally.

testimonial3.name: Jennifer A.
testimonial3.content: Thanks to the pilates program I started during pregnancy, I recovered very quickly after birth. My core muscles strengthened and my posture improved.

faq.question: What is the difference between clinical pilates and regular pilates?
faq.answer: Clinical pilates are programs designed specifically for your medical condition under the supervision of physiotherapists.

faq.question: Can I participate at a beginner level?
faq.answer: Yes, we have programs suitable for all levels. After the initial assessment, a suitable program for you will be determined.

faq.question: I have pain but want to come - can I participate?
faq.answer: Yes, you can participate. Clinical pilates conducted under physiotherapist supervision can be safely applied even in painful conditions.

faq.question: Is there an age scale for children?
faq.answer: Anyone who wants to develop their spine can benefit. Pilates conducted under physiotherapist supervision is beneficial for children.

whatIs.subtitle: What is Osteopathy?
whatIs.title: Natural Healing with Holistic Approach
whatIs.description1: Osteopathy is a holistic treatment approach that considers the body as a whole and supports its natural healing capacity. It corrects imbalances in the body using gentle manual techniques.
whatIs.description2: Our expert osteopaths provide long-term solutions by supporting your body's self-healing ability and improve your quality of life.

benefits.subtitle: Osteopathy Benefits
benefits.title: Why Choose Osteopathy?
benefits.description: Osteopathy helps you regain your health with a holistic approach.

holistic.title: Holistic Approach
holistic.description: Focuses on the entire body, not just symptoms, to find and treat the root cause of the problem.

natural.title: Natural Healing
natural.description: Activates the body's own healing mechanisms to provide natural and safe recovery.

painless.title: Painless Treatment
painless.description: Offers a comfortable and pleasant treatment experience with gentle and painless manual techniques.

expert.title: Expert Osteopath
expert.description: Receive reliable and professional treatment with our certified and experienced osteopaths.

techniques.subtitle: Treatment Methods

techniques.description: Regain your body's natural balance with modern osteopathy techniques.

structural.name: Structural Osteopathy
structural.description: Techniques that provide joint and muscle balance for musculoskeletal system problems

craniosacral.name: Craniosacral Therapy
craniosacral.description: Improves nervous system functions by regulating fluid flow between head and spine

visceral.name: Visceral Osteopathy
visceral.description: Supports digestive and respiratory systems by increasing mobility of internal organs

fascial.name: Fascial Release
fascial.description: Increases movement capacity by releasing tension in fascial tissues

process.description: We restore your body's natural balance with our professional osteopathy process.

faq.contactText: You can call us for your questions or contact us via WhatsApp.

duration.question: How long does osteopathy treatment take?
duration.answer: Treatment duration varies according to the complexity of your condition. Usually results are achieved between 4-8 sessions, chronic conditions may take longer.

sideEffects.question: Are there any side effects of osteopathy treatment?
sideEffects.answer: Osteopathy is a very safe treatment method. Mild fatigue or muscle sensitivity after treatment is normal and passes within 24-48 hours.

effectiveness.question: How effective is osteopathy?
effectiveness.answer: Osteopathy is highly effective for many musculoskeletal problems, headaches and stress-related disorders. Scientific studies show high success rates.

originalFaq.question: What kind of treatment method is osteopathy?
originalFaq.answer: Osteopathy is a holistic treatment approach that uses manual techniques and supports the body's natural healing capacity.

originalFaq.question: What conditions is it effective for?
originalFaq.answer: It is effective for musculoskeletal problems, headaches, digestive issues, and stress-related disorders.
